title: Lesson 8 - Choosing and Failing at Grounding: Scenarios, Trade-offs, and Failure Modes
description: Given a scenario, identify the appropriate grounding technique.

questions.question: A policy page changes daily and an agent must always state the current version. Which grounding approach fits?
options: A vector retriever over the policy documents
An action that reads the current record at run time rather than a retriever over an index
An ensemble retriever across all sources
A merge field on the case that stores a copy of the policy
questions.explanation: A retriever reads an index that refreshes on a schedule, so a fact that changes daily can be served stale, while an action that reads the record at run time always returns the current value.

questions.question: A retriever that returns every article in a huge library produces noisy answers. What is the best fix?
options: Rewrite the prompt to say ignore the irrelevant parts
Add a second retriever over the same index
Narrow the retriever to the right source and data space, filter by metadata, chunk by semantic boundary, and return only needed fields
questions.explanation: Over-broad retrieval is a configuration problem, so tightening the source, filters, chunking, and returned fields removes the noise, whereas a larger model or a prompt instruction does not fix a retrieval that returns the wrong passages.

questions.question: A scenario needs a single field value that already exists on the Contact record. Which grounding technique fits?
options: A merge field that references the record field
A vector retriever over contact documents
A Data Library over uploaded files
A prompt flow that recomputes the value each run
questions.explanation: A known field on the associated record is a merge field job, because the value already exists and a merge field pulls it deterministically, while a retriever or a flow adds complexity the scenario does not require.
